scope: Current-canonical admission of the qualified energy-conservation ledger and runtime-owned accepted-receipt association

invariants.evidence: One SWAP kernel remains authoritative; energy bookkeeping and runtime receipt ownership do not create a second kernel.
No file, parser, path, format or file-unit dependency is introduced into the kernel.
Energy transfers, storage snapshots, prepared trials, receipts and runtime results remain explicitly typed and separate from hydrologic committed state.
No energy-ledger or owner-receipt field is added to persistent kernel column state.
Receipt association and prepared energy-ledger state are transaction/runtime objects rather than permanent per-column solver scratch.
No storage-layout restriction is introduced; logical column identity remains runtime metadata.
Energy publication requires an accepted owned receipt from the exact physical commit; foreign, invalid and rejected receipts fail closed.
No committed physical initial state or warm-start semantics change; energy ledger work is candidate/receipt bound.
Energy trial and receipt provenance use generic t0/t1 intervals with no calendar or midnight assumption.
No fixed coupling-window duration is introduced.
Transactional exchange provenance is strengthened without weakening coupling rollback or commit ownership.
Groundwater head/flux interface semantics and sign convention are unchanged.
The energy ledger is not a water ledger; hydrologic mass accounting remains authoritative and is replayed under the admission gate.
No interface-sensitivity or response-tangent semantics change.
No structural extra SWAP solve is introduced by receipt association or energy bookkeeping.
MultiSWAP runtime column_id is the owner identity; no heavy solver instance or global owner registry is added per column.
No MODFLOW cell/tile fraction knowledge enters SWAP.
No deep-vadose component or state is introduced.
No deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition storage semantics change.
Soil-water solver interfaces remain unchanged and alternative solver implementations stay possible.
Existing hydrologic and bottom-energy results are reused; no duplicate crop, ET, drainage or soil-water physics is introduced.
The new modules use kernel/runtime contracts and do not depend on HeadCalc internals.
Receipt provenance is runtime transaction policy and does not silently modify physical options or solver policy.
No retry loop or unbounded computation is added; invalid ownership is rejected precommit.
Reference mode remains available and unchanged.
Fail-closed status and receipt readiness remain explicit and testable; existing solver and mass diagnostics are preserved.
No optional feature creates new persistent state for columns where it is unused.
Logical owner composition stays in runtime; generic F-KT/F-MR receipts remain column agnostic.
Owner identity and interval provenance are explicit; no legacy-file, daily-window or direct-MODFLOW assumption is added.
F-CI64 freezes exact authorities and production blobs, independently attacks cross-column aliasing, replays preservation paths and requires postimage reconciliation after promotion.
